hero.headline: Judge orders Trump name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to remove the president's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., ruling that only Congress has the authority to change the institution's official name.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper issued a 94-page opinion directing the Trump administration to take down all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days. "The Kennedy Center's organic statute makes crystal clear that the Center is to be named for President Kennedy, and it cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial based on the Board's unilateral say-so," Cooper wrote.

The controversy began when Trump appointed himself chair of the Kennedy Center's board of trustees in February, calling it a "take-over." He replaced board members with his own appointees. In December, the reconstituted board voted to add Trump's name to the institution, capping an aggressive effort to reshape Washington's arts and cultural institutions.

Cooper ruled that "the Board overstepped its statutory bounds by unilaterally renaming the Kennedy Center after President Trump." He emphasized that "Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it."

The lawsuit was brought by Joyce Beatty, an Ohio Democratic representative and board member. "The Kennedy Center is an institution that belongs to the American people, not to Donald Trump," Beatty said in response to the ruling.

The decision also temporarily blocked the Kennedy Center from closing this summer for proposed renovations, which Trump had announced in a two-year closure plan. Cooper found the board's decision to halt operations was "ill-informed and seemingly preordained," noting the board relied on insufficient information and failed to consider its full statutory obligations.

Trump responded through his Truth Social platform, stating he would work with Congress on transferring ownership of the Kennedy Center to the federal government. "Unless I am free to do what I do better than anyone else, bring this Institution back, physically, financially, and artistically, I have no interest in continuing what could only be a hopeless journey," Trump wrote.

The naming dispute prompted significant backlash within the arts community. Several performing groups canceled bookings in protest, including the Tony award-winning musical Hamilton. The National Symphony Orchestra's executive director left her position, and Richard Grenell, a Trump appointee who spearheaded efforts to overhaul the institution, stepped down as president.

The Kennedy Center, which receives federal funding, has long enjoyed bipartisan support as one of the nation's leading arts venues. The court's decision may set precedents for how future administrations can alter federally connected cultural institutions and national memorials.

cards.headline: Israel seizes Crusader castle in Lebanon as ground offensive expands
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a clifftop fortress overlooking southern Lebanon, in what marks the deepest military incursion into Lebanese territory in more than 26 years. Defense Minister Israel Katz confirmed the capture of the 12th-century stronghold, which Israel previously used as a military base during its occupation of southern Lebanon from 1982 to 2000.

The offensive represents a significant escalation in the conflict with Hezbollah. Israeli forces have already established control up to the Litani River and are now pushing toward the Zahrani River, approximately six miles further north. The Israel Defense Forces stated they launched the operation to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and expand territorial control in the region.

Video footage showed Israeli and Golani Brigade flags flying over Beaufort Castle as shelling continued in surrounding areas. The strategic location gives Israel command of much of southern Lebanon's landscape and appears designed to support a potential encirclement of Nabatieh, a major economic and cultural center in the south.

The military advance has drawn sharp international criticism. France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot requested an emergency UN Security Council meeting to address what he called unacceptable Israeli military operations. He stated that "nothing can justify the prolongation of Israeli military operations in Lebanon and its increasingly deep occupation of Lebanese territory."

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel on Saturday of pursuing a "scorched-earth policy and collective punishment," destroying towns and villages while forcing residents into exile. He called for an immediate ceasefire and warned that Israeli actions would not bring security or stability.

The escalation has complicated international negotiations. The advance threatens stalled talks between the United States and Iran, as Tehran has demanded that any agreement include an end to fighting in Lebanon. Regional observers suggest Israeli officials are attempting to inflict maximum damage on Hezbollah before potential diplomatic agreements impose new restrictions.

The conflict has already displaced more than 1.2 million people since March through Israeli strikes and evacuation orders. A ceasefire nominally began on April 17 but has not been observed, with both sides accusing each other of daily violations.

Some Israeli analysts question the military value of the castle seizure. Yagil Levy, head of the Institute for the Study of Civil-Military Relations at Open University of Israel, characterized the advance as primarily a "victory of image" rather than a meaningful strategic shift. He noted that criticism is emerging from within Israel's military about soldier vulnerability to drone attacks and that "Hezbollah remains intact" without a realistic disarmament plan.

Beaufort Castle holds deeper significance for Lebanon beyond its military position. Historically regarded as a symbol of resistance, it occupies an important place in southern Lebanon's political memory and cultural identity, having featured prominently in previous Israeli military campaigns.

cards.headline: U.S. military escorts 70 commercial ships through Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: U.S. Central Command has guided around 70 commercial vessels through the strait in the past three weeks as energy markets remain disrupted.
cards.body:
U.S. Central Command has facilitated the passage of approximately 70 commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz over the past three weeks, according to military officials. The strait serves as a vital corridor for global energy supplies, linking the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.

The escort operations underscore ongoing efforts to keep shipping lanes open through one of the world's most strategically important waterways. The missions occur amid broader regional tensions and continued volatility in energy markets.

cards.headline: Powell warns Federal Reserve credibility at risk in first remarks since leaving
cards.body:
Jerome Powell has issued a sharp warning about the Federal Reserve's credibility in his first public comments since stepping down as chair. Speaking while accepting the John F. Kennedy Profiles in Courage award on Sunday evening, Powell said the central bank faces a "stress test" and its credibility is on the line.

Though Powell did not explicitly name the Trump administration in his remarks, his message was unmistakable. He was responding to administration actions widely seen as attempts to undermine the Fed's independence, including a criminal investigation into the central bank's over-budget building renovation and efforts to remove governor Lisa Cook.

Powell framed threats to the Fed's independence as endangering an institution essential to American economic strength. His decision to use a high-profile award acceptance to issue this warning underscores how seriously he views the current situation.

The Federal Reserve has traditionally operated independently from political interference, a principle widely considered necessary for sound monetary policy. The criminal investigation into the building renovation marks an unusual escalation, as federal agencies typically handle budget overruns through administrative procedures rather than criminal probes.

Powell's term as Federal Reserve chair ended on May 15. However, he announced plans to remain on the Fed's board as a voting governor until the administration ends its scrutiny of the building renovation. Powell called this scrutiny "pretext" designed to pressure the central bank into lowering interest rates.

His departure comes as the Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the new Federal Reserve chair on Wednesday in a 54-45 vote split mostly along party lines. The confirmation was the most divisive for the position in history, with only Democratic senator John Fetterman from Pennsylvania joining Republicans in supporting Warsh's nomination.

Warsh, an Ivy League economist and former Wall Street banker, previously served as a Fed governor from 2006 to 2011. During his first stint on the board, he was known as an "inflation hawk" who advocated for higher interest rates to combat inflation. He departed the Fed board in 2011 partly due to disagreements over post-financial crisis stimulus measures.

Warsh will take office on May 14, taking over leadership at a time when inflation has climbed to 3.8% and the central bank faces intense pressure from the Trump administration to lower rates. A White House spokesperson called Warsh's confirmation "a welcome step towards finally restoring accountability, competence and confidence in Fed decision-making."

At his Senate confirmation hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and "take politics out of monetary policy." Yet his stated willingness to lower rates despite rising inflation, combined with his refusal to confirm that Trump lost the 2020 election, prompted Democrats to express concerns about his independence.

cards.headline: Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection
cards.teaser: The cases would mark the first infections outside Africa since the current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
Brazilian health authorities are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola virus infection. If laboratory tests confirm the disease, these would be the first cases detected outside Africa since the outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Ebola is a severe viral disease that spreads through contact with bodily fluids. The current outbreak has remained confined to the DRC, where health officials are working to contain the virus with community cooperation and support from the World Health Organization.

cards.headline: Trump seeks changes to US-Iran nuclear agreement
cards.teaser: The administration is requesting edits related to the Strait of Hormuz and uranium removal.
cards.body:
President Trump is seeking modifications to the US-Iran nuclear agreement, according to US media reports. The proposed changes focus on provisions concerning the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium from Iran.

These issues represent key areas of concern regarding Iran's nuclear capabilities and their potential military applications.

cards.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to acquire homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion
cards.body:
Berkshire Hathaway announced it will buy Taylor Morrison, a national homebuilder, for $6.8 billion in what marks the first major acquisition under the leadership of Greg Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett. Multiple sources reported the deal value as high as $8.5 billion when including debt. The acquisition represents a significant bet on the housing market by the Omaha-based conglomerate.

Taylor Morrison operates as one of the country's major homebuilders, constructing residential properties across multiple states. The company has been a publicly traded entity serving various housing market segments. Berkshire Hathaway already holds substantial real estate interests through its subsidiary HomeServices of America, one of the largest residential real estate brokerage networks in the United States.

The transaction comes at a time when the housing market faces uncertainty from elevated mortgage rates and affordability challenges. Berkshire's decision to make this investment signals confidence in the long-term fundamentals of residential construction despite near-term headwinds. The company has historically made contrarian bets during periods of market stress, often acquiring quality assets when valuations become more attractive.

This marks Abel's first major takeover since taking over from Buffett, who led Berkshire Hathaway for decades and built it into one of the world's most valuable companies through a combination of insurance operations, wholly owned businesses, and public market investments. Abel's approach to capital allocation and deal-making will be closely watched by investors as he shapes the company's strategy going forward.

The homebuilding industry has consolidated significantly over the past two decades, with larger builders gaining market share through economies of scale in land acquisition, construction, and financing. Berkshire's entry as a direct owner of a major homebuilder, rather than simply holding stocks of housing-related companies, represents a strategic shift in how the conglomerate is positioning itself in the residential real estate sector. The deal is expected to close following customary regulatory approvals and shareholder votes.

cards.headline: Colombia presidential election heads to runoff
cards.teaser: Left-wing senator Iván Cepeda will face Abelardo de la Espriella, an admirer of Trump, in the final ballot on June 21.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election will proceed to a runoff after no candidate secured a majority in the first round. Left-wing senator Iván Cepeda and far-right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella advanced to the final ballot scheduled for June 21. With nearly all ballots counted, Espriella received 43.7% of the vote while Cepeda garnered 40.9%.

Espriella, a Trump admirer, has positioned himself as a hardliner against drug cartels and represents a rising right-wing movement in Latin America. Cepeda, a philosopher and human rights activist who has served as a senator since 2014, is backed by the current leftist president Gustavo Petro. The runoff outcome could significantly reshape Colombia's political direction and its relationship with the United States.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russian oil infrastructure in overnight assault
cards.teaser: Drone attacks hit a pipeline, refinery, and fuel depot across multiple Russian regions as Ukraine continues targeting energy facilities.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces conducted overnight drone attacks against Russian energy infrastructure, targeting a pipeline, oil refinery, and fuel depot. The strikes damaged multiple facilities across different Russian regions.

Ukraine has indicated it will continue targeting Russian oil production and distribution sites within Russian territory as part of its military strategy. Russian sources reported the loss of a Tu-142MR aircraft during the overnight assault.

cards.headline: Nicaraguan indigenous leader dies after three years in detention
cards.teaser: Brooklyn Rivera, 73, died following what human rights groups describe as arbitrary imprisonment by the Nicaraguan government.
cards.body:
Brooklyn Rivera, a 73-year-old indigenous leader, has died following three years in prison in Nicaragua. Rights groups have condemned his lengthy detention by the government as arbitrary.

His death underscores concerns about political repression in Nicaragua, with international observers documenting a pattern of detentions under the current administration. Rivera's case reflects broader criticism of how the governing regime has treated opposition figures and indigenous leaders.

cards.headline: 2025 wildfires set record as costliest year for fire damage
cards.teaser: Severe blazes in densely populated areas including Los Angeles drove record financial losses last year, researchers say.
cards.body:
Researchers have confirmed that 2025 saw the most expensive wildfire damage in recorded history. Severe blazes that proved challenging to contain in densely populated areas, particularly around Los Angeles, drove these unprecedented financial losses.

The record-breaking costs reflect how wildfires increasingly threaten urban and suburban communities rather than remaining isolated to remote regions. The combination of fire intensity and concentrated property development in affected areas significantly amplified the total value of destroyed assets.

cards.headline: UK bans entry of American political commentators Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker
cards.teaser: The left-wing YouTube personalities were barred from entering the United Kingdom over their criticism of Israel.
cards.body:
British authorities have prohibited American political commentators Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker from entering the United Kingdom. The bans appear connected to the commentators' public criticism of Israel and their positions on Middle Eastern politics.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump physical exam results
cards.teaser: President Trump's physician says he is in excellent health and recommends weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
The White House released results from President Trump's latest physical examination. His doctor stated that Trump is in excellent health but recommended that he lose weight and increase his exercise routine.

The medical readout left some information unspecified, according to reports. The physical exam is part of standard protocol for sitting presidents, providing the public with basic health information about the commander in chief.

cards.teaser: The administration is requesting edits related to the Strait of Hormuz and uranium removal.
cards.body:
President Trump is seeking modifications to the US-Iran nuclear agreement, according to US media reports. The proposed changes focus on provisions concerning the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium from Iran.

These issues represent key areas of concern regarding Iran's nuclear capabilities and their potential military applications.

cards.headline: Platner acknowledges sending sexual texts while married
cards.teaser: The Maine Senate candidate's campaign confirms he sent sexually explicit messages to women during his marriage.
cards.body:
Graham Platner's Senate campaign in Maine confirmed that the Democratic candidate sent sexually explicit text messages to women while married. His wife reportedly alerted his campaign staff to the messages.

Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey expressed concerns about Platner's candidacy, stating that "that guy has questions to answer." Booker made the comments on ABC's This Week, suggesting the campaign process itself would be where those questions could be addressed. The controversy impacts Democratic hopes to flip Maine's Senate seat in what was already considered a competitive race.

cards.headline: New York Mayor Mamdani skips Israel Day parade
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani breaks with tradition by not attending the annual Fifth Avenue event.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the annual Israel Day Parade on Fifth Avenue, departing from a longstanding mayoral tradition. Previous New York mayors have typically attended the event as a show of support for the city's Jewish community and US-Israel relations.

The parade drew thousands of spectators and is an annual fixture in New York City's cultural calendar. Far-right Israeli ministers participated in the celebration.

cards.headline: Aid cuts strain Ebola crisis response in Uganda
cards.teaser: Health workers prepare for potential spread from Democratic Republic of Congo as funding shrinks.
cards.body:
Aid workers in Uganda are monitoring a rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo, with cases already reaching the Ugandan capital Kampala. However, foreign aid cuts are hampering their ability to respond effectively to the crisis.

The situation is particularly challenging in Ituri province, the outbreak's epicenter, where crowded mining operations and ongoing armed conflict create ideal conditions for transmission. Displaced populations in overcrowded camps and limited medical facilities further complicate containment efforts. Health officials warn that reduced global support makes a prolonged crisis increasingly likely.

cards.headline: US-Iran conflict strike hits Sri Lankan coastal town
cards.teaser: A deadly attack during the early days of the Iran war reached the Indian Ocean.
cards.body:
A deadly strike connected to the US-Iran conflict reached a coastal town in Sri Lanka during the early days of the war. The attack demonstrated how the conflict's impact extends far beyond the Middle East, reaching the Indian Ocean island nation thousands of miles away.

The strike jolted the quiet seaside community, bringing the distant conflict directly to residents with no involvement in the hostilities. The incident illustrated the geographic scope of the US-Iran tensions and their ability to affect civilian populations globally.

cards.headline: Former Fed Chair Jerome Powell warns Fed credibility at risk from political interference
cards.teaser: Powell cautioned that the Federal Reserve's credibility would be lost if presidents could fire central bank officials.
cards.body:
Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell warned that the central bank's credibility is at risk and would be lost if presidents gained the ability to fire Fed officials. Powell, who previously led the institution, delivered the warning in what was described as pointed language wrapped in abstraction. His comments addressed concerns about the politicization of the Federal Reserve.

The warning comes amid broader debates about the independence of the central bank and its role in setting monetary policy. Powell emphasized that public trust in the Fed depends on its ability to operate independently from political pressure. The Federal Reserve has historically maintained independence from the executive branch to make decisions based on economic data rather than political considerations.

cards.headline: Oil prices climb as U.S.-Iran agreement remains out of reach
cards.teaser: Oil markets rose after recording their biggest one-month drop in six years, with the Strait of Hormuz showing few signs of reopening.
cards.body:
Oil prices increased as negotiations between the United States and Iran have not yet produced an agreement. The climb came after oil recorded its biggest one-month drop in six years, providing some relief to consumers. Brent crude posted its largest monthly loss in six years as markets had anticipated a potential U.S.-Iran deal.

Despite the recent decline, oil prices rose amid continued uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping channel for global energy supplies. U.S. crude futures rose $2.53 to $89.89 per barrel. The dollar also climbed alongside oil as markets assessed the ongoing geopolitical situation and its impact on energy supplies.

cards.headline: Wall Street prepares for SpaceX public offering
cards.teaser: The upcoming SpaceX IPO, scheduled for June 12, is forcing investment banks to reorganize their approach to the space sector.
cards.body:
SpaceX's planned initial public offering is prompting Wall Street firms to reorganize their operations around the highly anticipated event. The space exploration company founded by Elon Musk is set to go public on June 12, according to multiple reports. The IPO is drawing significant attention from investors and analysts across the financial sector.

The offering has sparked broader interest in space-related stocks, with analysts highlighting other companies in the sector worth watching. Concerns have been raised about governance risks for potential SpaceX IPO buyers, while some market observers have questioned whether sky-high IPO pricing serves the interests of retail investors. The deal represents one of the most significant public offerings in recent years.

cards.headline: Stock futures hold steady as markets open June near record highs
cards.teaser: U.S. stock futures were flat in overnight trading as June began with major indexes at or near record levels.
cards.body:
Stock futures remained largely flat in overnight trading as Wall Street began June with major indexes near record highs. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq closed May with strong performances, extending recent market gains into the new month.

Oil prices rose in early trading while equity futures stayed relatively unchanged. Investors are watching for upcoming economic data releases, including U.S. payrolls figures, which could influence market direction in the coming weeks.

hero.headline: Dell launches $599 XPS 13 laptop to compete with Apple's MacBook Neo
hero.body:
Dell has announced a new XPS 13 laptop designed to challenge Apple's recently launched MacBook Neo. The device will be available at a promotional price of $599 for students during its July launch, with the offer running through September for back-to-school shoppers. After the promotional period ends, the laptop will cost $699 for general consumers.

The timing of Dell's announcement follows the MacBook Neo's introduction, Apple's first entry-level MacBook priced at $599. The MacBook Neo runs on an A18 Pro chip, the same processor found in iPhone 16 Pro models, and includes 8GB of RAM with either 256GB or 512GB storage options. Apple positioned the device as an accessible entry point to its MacBook lineup, priced $500 below the MacBook Air.

Dell's XPS 13 strategy appears focused on offering competitive specifications at similar price points. The company is leveraging its XPS line's reputation as a premium consumer laptop series to attract buyers who might consider Apple's offering. By introducing a temporary discount, Dell aims to build momentum during the critical back-to-school season when students make purchasing decisions.

The MacBook Neo features a 13-inch LCD screen with 2408x1506 resolution and 500-nit brightness, delivering crisp visuals comparable to Apple's more expensive models. The device maintains the company's design language with an aluminum body, rounded corners, and quality construction throughout. Despite its lower price, the Neo includes a mechanical trackpad that reviewers noted performs well, plus a headphone jack that remains uncommon on modern laptops.

Performance testing shows the Neo handles everyday tasks effectively, including complex photo editing in professional applications and light video editing. Battery life reaches approximately 13 hours during typical work activities like browsing, note-taking, and email. The machine runs macOS 26 Tahoe and comes with Apple's bundled software suite including Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Garage Band, and iMovie.

The MacBook Neo does include some trade-offs for its price. It lacks a Touch ID fingerprint scanner on the base model, a feature only available on the higher-priced 512GB variant. The screen is smaller at 13 inches compared to the 13.6-inch Air display, and lacks True Tone technology. The device includes two USB-C ports but only one supports USB3, limiting connectivity options. It cannot drive high refresh rate displays and won't work with certain docks requiring Thunderbolt support.

Dell's response indicates the premium ultraportable laptop market remains competitive as manufacturers vie for consumer attention. The XPS 13's positioning at the same price point as Apple's entry-level MacBook suggests Dell recognizes the significance of Apple's push into budget-conscious segments. The temporary discount strategy represents an aggressive approach to establishing market presence in a segment where Apple has gained considerable ground in recent years.

cards.headline: Alienware unveils 39-inch 5K OLED gaming monitor with RGB stripe panel
cards.teaser: Dell's Alienware division has released the AW3926QW, the first 39-inch gaming monitor featuring 5K resolution and an RGB stripe OLED panel.
cards.body:
The Alienware AW3926QW is the world's first 39-inch 5K OLED gaming monitor with an RGB stripe panel. This new ultrawide display marks a significant expansion of Alienware's OLED gaming monitor lineup.

Alienware announced the monitor at Computex 2026 in Taipei alongside new 34-inch OLED gaming options. These releases represent upgrades to Alienware's existing QD-OLED monitors, which the company originally introduced in 2022 and established as a category for premium gaming displays.

cards.headline: Apple prepares iOS 27 release with overhauled Siri and AI features
cards.teaser: Apple is preparing to release iOS 27 with significant changes to Siri and artificial intelligence capabilities ahead of its WWDC 2026 conference.
cards.body:
Apple plans to overhaul Siri and AI features in iOS 27, according to reports ahead of the company's Worldwide Developers Conference in 2026. The update represents a significant revision to the iPhone operating system's voice assistant and machine learning capabilities.

The company is expected to showcase iOS 27 at WWDC 2026, where it typically previews the next version of its mobile operating system before releasing it to the public later in the year. Apple has not yet announced a specific release date for the software update.

cards.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 set for October release with Korean war setting
cards.teaser: Activision has announced Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, featuring a present-day Korean war scenario and launching October 23 with campaign, multiplayer, and DMZ modes.
cards.body:
The next Call of Duty game launches October 23 with a campaign set during a contemporary Korean conflict. Modern Warfare 4 will feature campaign, multiplayer, and DMZ modes, marking the series' debut on Nintendo Switch 2.

Infinity Ward is positioning the game as a return to grounded, controversial storytelling after years of melodramatic campaigns. The developer emphasizes military authenticity while tackling a politically sensitive real-world setting—a notable shift for a franchise that has historically courted controversy through its narrative choices.

cards.headline: Artist KC Green reaches agreement with AI startup over 'This is fine' meme use
cards.teaser: KC Green, creator of the This is fine meme, has reached an agreement with AI startup Artisan after the company used the image in advertising.
cards.body:
Artisan, an artificial intelligence startup, has taken down advertisements that used KC Green's This is fine meme following an agreement with the artist. The meme, featuring a dog sitting calmly in a burning room, has become one of the internet's most recognizable images.

The settlement comes after Green objected to the unauthorized commercial use of his work.

cards.headline: Environmental activist Erin Brockovich targets data center secrecy
cards.teaser: Erin Brockovich has launched a new campaign focused on transparency issues surrounding data centers.
cards.body:
Environmental activist Erin Brockovich, known for her work on groundwater contamination cases, has shifted focus to data center operations and their environmental impact. Brockovich is targeting what she describes as secrecy around data center practices.

The campaign represents a new direction for Brockovich, who gained prominence for her investigation into water pollution in California. Data centers have come under increasing scrutiny for their energy consumption and environmental footprint.

cards.headline: ASUS prepares to unveil new ROG Ally gaming handheld at Computex
cards.teaser: ASUS is expected to preview a next-generation ROG Ally gaming handheld at Computex 2026, according to leaked information.
cards.body:
Leaked information suggests ASUS will showcase a new ROG Xbox Ally gaming handheld at Computex 2026. The device would be a successor to the company's existing portable gaming hardware.

ASUS has announced plans to preview next-generation AI and consumer computing products at Computex 2026. The company is also expected to show a golden-black ROG Astral RTX 50 Series graphics card as part of its ROG 20th Anniversary Edition lineup.

hero.headline: Knicks and Spurs to meet in NBA Finals rematch of 1999
hero.body:
The New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs will face off in the NBA Finals after both teams secured their conference championships. The Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in a Game 7 victory in the Western Conference finals, while the Knicks swept the Cleveland Cavaliers 4-0 in the Eastern Conference finals to advance to their first championship series since 1999.

The Knicks' path through the playoffs has been dominant. They swept the Philadelphia 76ers in the conference semifinals and beat the Atlanta Hawks 4-1 in the first round. Against Cleveland, New York won by margins of 16, 13 and 37 points before completing the sweep with a 130-93 victory on Monday night. The team is currently riding an 11-game playoff winning streak, the third longest in NBA postseason history.

Jalen Brunson has been the standout performer for New York. The guard won the Eastern Conference finals MVP award after averaging 25.5 points and 7.8 assists across the series. Brunson, whose father Rick played for the Knicks during their last Finals appearance in 1999, acknowledged his teammates' contributions after the sweep was completed. "I wouldn't be here without my teammates, my coach, this staff, the fanbase. Without them none of this is possible," Brunson said.

Karl-Anthony Towns contributed 19 points and 14 rebounds in Monday's clinching game, while Cleveland's Donovan Mitchell scored 31 points but could not lead a serious challenge against the high-flying Knicks. "They're playing better basketball. You got to give them credit. They're on a heater," Cleveland coach Kenny Atkinson said.

The Spurs' advance was anchored by 7-foot-4 superstar Victor Wembanyama, who led San Antonio past Oklahoma City in the Western Conference finals. The Thunder had been viewed as nearly flawless for much of the season, but Wembanyama proved to be the deciding factor in the series.

Game 1 of the Finals will be held Wednesday in San Antonio. The first Knicks home game will take place June 8, with courtside seats already commanding premium prices of $105,000 on resale sites.

The 1999 Finals saw the Spurs defeat the Knicks in five games during a lockout-shortened season. That series marked San Antonio's first championship and launched a dynasty producing multiple titles. For the Knicks, the loss began a 53-year title drought, with their last championship coming in 1973.

The Knicks' fanbase has shown tremendous support. High-profile fans including Spike Lee, Tracy Morgan and Timothée Chalamet traveled to Cleveland for Monday's game. Guard Landry Shamet remarked on the passionate supporters: "Knicks fans fly out to Cleveland on a Monday, they're everywhere. The buzz is unbelievable."

cards.headline: Marta Kostyuk eliminates four-time champion Iga Swiatek at French Open
cards.teaser: Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk defeated defending champion Iga Swiatek at the French Open, guaranteeing a first-time women's champion.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk delivered a stunning upset, defeating four-time French Open champion Iga Swiatek in the round of 16. The victory on Kostyuk's birthday eliminated the last remaining former champion from the women's draw, guaranteeing that a new winner will be crowned at Roland Garros this year.

The result marked a significant moment for Ukrainian tennis, with Kostyuk advancing to face fellow countryman Elina Svitolina in an all-Ukrainian quarterfinal. Both players progressed on the same day, highlighting a strong showing for Ukraine at the tournament.

cards.headline: Finland wins ice hockey world championship on Konsta Helenius overtime goal
cards.teaser: Konsta Helenius scored in overtime to give Finland the world championship title at the IIHF tournament.
cards.body:
Finland captured the IIHF World Championship after Konsta Helenius scored the golden goal in overtime. The 19-year-old's heroics delivered Finland its latest international title in ice hockey, adding to the nation's storied history in the sport.

Roman Josi was named the tournament's most valuable player and selected to the All-Star team as best defender despite his team not winning the championship. Florida Panthers forwards Aleksander Barkov and Anton Lundell both won gold medals as members of the Finnish squad, adding to their NHL success.

cards.headline: Illinois lawmakers pursue new stadium deal to keep Bears in state
cards.teaser: Lawmakers drafted a backup proposal after the Arlington Heights PILOT plan for a Chicago Bears stadium collapsed.
cards.body:
Illinois legislators are working on an alternative proposal to keep the Chicago Bears in the state after plans for an Arlington Heights stadium development collapsed. The original arrangement, which included a payment in lieu of taxes agreement, fell through, prompting lawmakers to develop backup options.

With time running short, multiple legislative proposals are being considered to finalize terms that would prevent the franchise from relocating. Officials are racing to present a deal that satisfies both the team and state interests.

cards.headline: United States defeats Senegal 3-2 in World Cup preparation match
cards.teaser: Christian Pulisic broke his goal drought as the US men's national team won a pre-World Cup friendly.
cards.body:
Christian Pulisic ended a nearly six-month goal drought in the United States' 3-2 victory over Senegal on Sunday in Charlotte, North Carolina. Sergiño Dest opened the scoring just seven minutes into the match, while Pulisic both assisted on the opening goal and scored himself in the first half.

Sadio Mané led Senegal's comeback with two goals, but the US held on for the win. The friendly marked the start of World Cup preparations for the co-hosts, with a final tune-up scheduled against Germany in Chicago on June 6.

cards.headline: North Carolina advances to baseball super regional after defeating East Carolina
cards.teaser: The Tar Heels won the Chapel Hill Regional with a 9-3 victory over East Carolina to reach their 13th super regional.
cards.body:
North Carolina defeated East Carolina 9-3 in the regional final to advance to the NCAA baseball super regionals. The victory was the Tar Heels' 13th appearance in the super regional round.

The game took place in Chapel Hill, with North Carolina securing the elimination matchup to end East Carolina's tournament run. The Tar Heels will now host a super regional series as they continue their pursuit of reaching the College World Series.

cards.headline: Joao Fonseca reaches French Open quarterfinals with win over Casper Ruud
cards.teaser: The 19-year-old tennis player defeated two-time finalist Casper Ruud to advance to the final eight at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Rising star Joao Fonseca has demonstrated his championship credentials by defeating two-time French Open finalist Casper Ruud to advance to the quarterfinals. The 19-year-old's impressive run follows his earlier victory against Novak Djokovic, signaling his emergence as a genuine contender in Paris.

With no previous French Open champions remaining in the draw—including Iga Swiatek's early exit—the tournament is wide open. Fonseca now has an opportunity to capitalize on the disrupted field as he pushes deeper into the competition.

hero.headline: R&B Singer Peabo Bryson Suffers Stroke
hero.body:
Veteran R&B singer Peabo Bryson has suffered a stroke and is receiving treatment, according to a statement from his representative. The two-time Grammy Award winner is best known for his duets on Disney film soundtracks, including the Oscar-winning songs from Aladdin and Beauty and the Beast.

Bryson's representative confirmed the stroke in a statement but did not provide additional details about his condition or prognosis. The singer has been a fixture in R&B music for decades, earning recognition for his smooth vocal style and romantic ballads.

The artist achieved widespread fame through his Disney collaborations, particularly A Whole New World from Aladdin, performed with Regina Belle, and the title track from Beauty and the Beast, performed with Celine Dion. Both songs won Academy Awards for Best Original Song and became defining moments in his career. His work on these soundtracks introduced his voice to new generations of listeners beyond his established R&B audience.

Bryson's career spans multiple decades, during which he released numerous albums and charted several hits in the R&B and adult contemporary genres. His collaborations with other artists, including Roberta Flack, helped cement his status as one of the premier romantic singers of his generation. He won Grammy Awards for his duets, showcasing his ability to blend his voice seamlessly with other performers.

The news of his stroke comes as the music community continues to monitor the health of several veteran performers. Bryson's contributions to both R&B music and film soundtracks have left a lasting impact on popular culture, with his Disney songs remaining staples at weddings and romantic occasions. His representatives have not announced any updates on his recovery timeline or future performance plans.

cards.headline: Matt Brown of Alaskan Bush People Found Dead at 42
cards.teaser: Matt Brown, star of the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 42.
cards.body:
Matt Brown, known for his role on the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, was found dead. His family confirmed his death, and his brother Noah Brown helped pull his body from a river. The family announced the news through various media outlets.

Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People, which followed his family living off the grid in Alaska and later in Washington state. He had been open about personal struggles during his time on the show. His brother Noah confirmed he identified the body after it was recovered from the river.

cards.headline: M.I.A. Sues Kid Cudi for $2.8 Million Over Tour Removal
cards.teaser: British rapper M.I.A. filed a lawsuit against Kid Cudi seeking $2.8 million after being removed from his Rebel Ragers Tour.
cards.body:
M.I.A. is suing Kid Cudi for $2.8 million after being kicked off the Rebel Ragers Tour. The British rapper was removed from the tour following what Kid Cudi described as offensive remarks during her opening act performances. A statement from M.I.A.'s team said Kid Cudi's attempts to silence freedom of artistic expression and speech on his tour cannot go unchallenged.

The lawsuit names Kid Cudi and appears to involve M.I.A.'s contract with Live Nation, which she claims guaranteed her full creative control over her performances. The legal action centers on the termination of her role as opening act on the tour, which M.I.A. characterizes as a breach of her artistic freedom.

cards.headline: Backrooms Opens With $81 Million at Box Office
cards.teaser: The film Backrooms, based on an online phenomenon, debuted with $81 million at the box office.
cards.body:
Backrooms, a film based on an internet obsession, opened with $81 million at the box office in its debut weekend. The strong performance represents a notable success for content originating from online culture. Multiple media outlets described the opening as stunning and characterized it as marking a turning point for Hollywood.

The film's success comes as YouTube creators and internet-native content increasingly influence the movie business. Analysts suggested the performance of Backrooms and other recent films could change the future of moviemaking, with some comparing the shift to a transformation of the traditional film industry. The box office results exceeded industry expectations for the adaptation.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Delivers Freestyle Dissing Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj
cards.teaser: Jay-Z performed a surprise freestyle rap targeting Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj at the Roots Picnic festival.
cards.body:
Jay-Z delivered an unannounced a cappella freestyle performance at the Roots Picnic festival that included diss tracks aimed at fellow rappers Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj. The performance took place during the festival and caught attendees by surprise.

The freestyle marked a departure from typical festival performances, with Jay-Z choosing to perform without instrumental backing. The specific content of the disses directed at the three artists was described as fiery, though the exact lyrics were not detailed in initial reports.

cards.headline: DirecTV Drops 54 Scripps Local TV Stations in Contract Dispute
cards.teaser: Fifty-four local television stations owned by Scripps went dark on DirecTV as a retransmission fee dispute escalated.
cards.body:
Scripps and DirecTV are locked in a retransmission battle that resulted in 54 local Scripps stations going dark on DirecTV as of 7 p.m. ET. The blackout affects 36 Nielsen-designated markets across the country. Both companies blamed each other for the failure to reach an agreement.

DirecTV noted the timing of the blackout comes just before several state and local primary elections scheduled for June, as well as upcoming NBA playoffs. The dispute centers on the fees DirecTV pays to carry Scripps-owned local stations, a common source of conflict between broadcasters and pay-TV providers.

cards.headline: WWE Announces King and Queen of the Ring Tournament Brackets
cards.teaser: WWE revealed the brackets for its 2026 King and Queen of the Ring tournaments.
cards.body: WWE unveiled the brackets for the 2026 King and Queen of the Ring tournaments. The Queen of the Ring bracket

hero.headline: Powell warns Federal Reserve credibility at risk in first remarks since leaving
hero.body:
Jerome Powell has issued a sharp warning about the Federal Reserve's credibility in his first public comments since stepping down as chair. Speaking while accepting the John F. Kennedy Profiles in Courage award on Sunday evening, Powell said the central bank faces a "stress test" and its credibility is on the line.

Though Powell did not explicitly name the Trump administration in his remarks, his message was unmistakable. He was responding to administration actions widely seen as attempts to undermine the Fed's independence, including a criminal investigation into the central bank's over-budget building renovation and efforts to remove governor Lisa Cook.

Powell framed threats to the Fed's independence as endangering an institution essential to American economic strength. His decision to use a high-profile award acceptance to issue this warning underscores how seriously he views the current situation.

The Federal Reserve has traditionally operated independently from political interference, a principle widely considered necessary for sound monetary policy. The criminal investigation into the building renovation marks an unusual escalation, as federal agencies typically handle budget overruns through administrative procedures rather than criminal probes.

Powell's term as Federal Reserve chair ended on May 15. However, he announced plans to remain on the Fed's board as a voting governor until the administration ends its scrutiny of the building renovation. Powell called this scrutiny "pretext" designed to pressure the central bank into lowering interest rates.

His departure comes as the Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the new Federal Reserve chair on Wednesday in a 54-45 vote split mostly along party lines. The confirmation was the most divisive for the position in history, with only Democratic senator John Fetterman from Pennsylvania joining Republicans in supporting Warsh's nomination.

Warsh, an Ivy League economist and former Wall Street banker, previously served as a Fed governor from 2006 to 2011. During his first stint on the board, he was known as an "inflation hawk" who advocated for higher interest rates to combat inflation. He departed the Fed board in 2011 partly due to disagreements over post-financial crisis stimulus measures.

Warsh will take office on May 14, taking over leadership at a time when inflation has climbed to 3.8% and the central bank faces intense pressure from the Trump administration to lower rates. A White House spokesperson called Warsh's confirmation "a welcome step towards finally restoring accountability, competence and confidence in Fed decision-making."

At his Senate confirmation hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and "take politics out of monetary policy." Yet his stated willingness to lower rates despite rising inflation, combined with his refusal to confirm that Trump lost the 2020 election, prompted Democrats to express concerns about his independence.

cards.headline: Macron urges Middle East leaders to support US-Iran deal
cards.teaser: French President Emmanuel Macron called for regional support of US-Iran negotiations after months of conflict closed the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron urged Middle East leaders to seize the current opportunity for a U.S.-Iran peace deal. His diplomatic push came following months of conflict that led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route with significant global economic consequences.

Macron met with regional leaders including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, and Emirati officials to advance negotiations. The closure of the strategic waterway underscores the urgency of reaching an agreement between the United States and Iran.

cards.headline: Trump says departure of 10,000 federal lawyers is good for administration
cards.teaser: President Trump defended the loss of thousands of government attorneys, saying their exit benefits his administration.
cards.body:
President Trump responded to a New York Times report on the mass departure of federal lawyers by calling the exodus very good. The Times reported that more than 10,000 lawyers working for the federal government have left their positions between the end of 2024 and March.

Trump's comments frame the significant loss of legal talent as a positive development for his administration. The departures represent a substantial reduction in the government's legal workforce across multiple agencies and departments.

cards.headline: Paxton to meet Senate leadership after defeating Cornyn in GOP primary
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton will meet with Senate Majority Leader John Thune after winning the Republican runoff against incumbent Senator John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said he will meet with Senate Majority Leader John Thune following his victory in the GOP runoff to replace incumbent Senator John Cornyn. Paxton defeated Cornyn, a four-term incumbent, in the Republican primary contest.

Paxton said he has been in contact with Thune, Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, and Republican Conference Chair since winning the runoff. The meetings will focus on his transition to the Senate and his role within the Republican caucus.

cards.headline: DNC Chair Martin faces growing pressure over 2024 election review and finances
cards.teaser: Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin confronts mounting criticism over the party's handling of its 2024 election analysis and budget issues.
cards.body:
Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin faces increasing criticism over the party's handling of its 2024 election review and financial troubles. The controversy represents the biggest early test of Democratic leadership as the party prepares for the 2028 presidential election.

Martin has so far avoided a revolt among DNC members as they work on setting the calendar for the 2028 presidential primary. Critics within the party say the DNC bungled its analysis of what went wrong in 2024 while also struggling with financial management.

cards.headline: New Jersey resumes family visits at immigration detention center after protests
cards.teaser: Governor Mikie Sherrill announced the Department of Homeland Security will restore visitation rights at Delaney Hall Detention Center following demonstrations.
cards.body:
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and the Department of Homeland Security announced on Sunday that family visitation would be restored at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark. The resumption comes after a week of heated protests at the facility, which were triggered when detainees began a hunger strike.

The restoration of visits is only partial, and families received conflicting information about which detainees would be eligible for visitation. Local officials also imposed an indefinite overnight curfew beginning at 9pm in a blocked-off area surrounding Delaney Hall.

cards.headline: Pence says efforts underway to rewrite January 6 history
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence said there has been a clear effort to alter the historical record of the Capitol riot.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Sunday that there has been a clear effort to rewrite the history of the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot. Pence expressed confidence in how history will ultimately judge his actions and those of others involved that day.

His comments touch on ongoing disputes about how the events should be characterized and remembered. Pence referenced both the Capitol Police response during the riot and the lawmakers who returned to the Capitol afterward to complete the electoral certification process.
